document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Standards
notes: International organization founded Paris 1929 (Union Internationale des Concierges d'Hotels — UICH). Annual signed oath required. Conflict-of-interest rules (no restaurant commissions). Guest and employer confidentiality. Vendor integrity standards. Motto: 'In Service Through Friendship.'

ALP is the successor organization to PAII (Professional Association of Innkeepers International, est. 1987) + AIHP merger. Aspirational code crafted with association law counsel. All membership categories required to consent. Covers duties to guests, employees, vendors, the Association, and the public.

Policy Manual revised September 2023. Six areas: Ethics and Transparency, Embracing Diversity, Anti-harassment, Business Relationships (no human trafficking), Sustainability. Straddles Div 55 (hotel meetings) and Div 56 (event catering) — classified under 55.

document_title: Principles of Professional and Ethical Conduct
notes: Represents highest levels of professional and ethical behavior in convention industry. Core principles: integrity, respect, honesty, credibility. Continuing education and knowledge-sharing obligations. Conflict-of-interest avoidance. CMP (Certified Meeting Professional) holders reference this code.

profession_name: Business Travel Manager / Corporate Travel Professional
notes: National GBTA code implemented at chapter level. Austin chapter document is most publicly accessible. Key provisions: good faith dealings, buyer privacy, fair competition, client confidentiality, professional growth. Violations may result in membership suspension or revocation.

Applies to all full members AND all ACF-certified individuals (CEC, CC, CPC, CCA, CEPC, etc. — multiple certification levels). 20,000+ members. Non-discrimination, safety, professional development, accurate credentials representation. Direct PDF hosted on acfchefs.org.

organization: National Association for Catering and Events
notes: Formal Ethics Review Procedures with Ethics Complaint Form submitted to ethics@nace.net. Covers inclusion (race, religion, national origin, age, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, political affiliation). Members take responsibility for advancing NACE mission and the profession.

document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Responsibility
notes: May 2021 version. Signed as eligibility condition for all CMS-A programming. Core values: Hospitality, Integrity, Humility, Self-Care, Diversity. Diversity and harassment training modules required. Anonymous reporting available. Whistleblower protections.

Core values: Service, Integrity, Sharing Knowledge, Tradition, Camaraderie. Comprehensive anti-discrimination and anti-harassment provisions. Misconduct investigation procedures with membership suspension as remedy. Applies to all in-person and online USBG activities.
